children: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission began its annual Article IV consultations with Oman on Sunday, with discussions set to continue until November 8, focusing on economic prospects, fiscal and monetary policies, financial sector development and structural reforms.

The mission is being hosted by the Central Bank of Oman (CBO) and the Ministry of Finance as part of the periodic consultations required under Article IV of the IMF’s Articles of Agreement. It follows a preparatory visit by an IMF delegation from June 7 to 15, 2026.

During the visit, the IMF team will meet officials from the CBO, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Economy, National Centre for Statistics and Information, Ministry of Labour, Tax Authority and Oman Investment Authority. Discussions will also involve other government entities, representatives of the private and banking sectors, and civil society organisations.

The consultations will provide the Fund with an opportunity to assess Oman’s latest economic and financial developments, evaluate the outlook and discuss policy priorities with government officials and other stakeholders.
Technical discussions will cover fiscal and monetary policies, financial sector development, structural reforms and progress towards the objectives of Oman Vision 2040.

Economic diversification, public and private investment, job creation and private sector growth are also among the key areas of focus, alongside efforts to strengthen the economy’s sustainability and resilience to global developments.

The Article IV consultations form part of the IMF’s regular economic surveillance of its member countries, providing a framework for dialogue on macroeconomic conditions, policy challenges and opportunities for sustainable growth.
